questions.question: How does Zustand work and why would you choose it over Redux or Context?
questions.title: Zustand Basics
questions.direct_answer: Zustand creates a store OUTSIDE React: create(set => ({...state, actions})) returns hooks that components call to read slices. Updates go through set (which merges shallowly). Components subscribe via selectors — only components whose selected slice changed re-render. Choose it when you want global state with Redux-like selector re-render control but Redux-level ceremony: no Provider, no boilerplate, ~1KB, actions are plain functions in the store.

sections.title: Interview Answer
Mental Model
sections.content:
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    S[create: store + actions] --> H[hook: useStore selector]
    H --> C1[component A: count slice]
    H --> C2[component B: addItem slice]
    U[set called] --> N[notify listeners]
    N -->|slice changed| R1[A re-renders]
    N -->|slice unchanged| R2[B skipped - selector equality]
    subgraph vs-context
        CTX[context value change] --> ALL[ALL consumers re-render]
    end
```

sections.title: Deep Dive
sections.content:
The subscription machinery (the internals worth knowing): Zustand is a tiny pub-sub — create returns a hook bound to a module-level store; each selector-subscribing component registers a listener. On set, listeners run; each compares its selected value with the previous (Object.is by default); changed → schedule that component's re-render; unchanged → nothing. This is useSyncExternalStore underneath (the React 18 API for external stores) — the same mechanism React itself uses to subscribe to foreign state sources, which is why it's concurrent-rendering-safe.

The composability layer (the scale-up answers): multiple stores by domain (useCart, useAuth, useUI) instead of one god-store — each independent, tree-shakeable, testable in isolation. Middleware for cross-cutting: persist (localStorage/sessionStorage sync), devtools (Redux DevTools integration — time travel works), immer (mutator-style syntax compiled to immutable updates), subscribeWithSelector (finer-grained subscriptions than the default equality). Slices compose via combining partial stores — the pattern for teams wanting domain separation without full microstores.

The honest boundaries (when Redux still wins): large organizations value enforced conventions (action logs as audit trails, a single dispatch pipeline for middleware like analytics/auth guards), RTK Query's server-cache integration, and the mature ecosystem. Zustand is a tool for small-to-mid apps and teams that trust conventions over enforcement — the trade is explicit: less structure, less safety net, more speed. Naming that trade is what makes the answer senior rather than tribal.
